prompt: Using the commuting table, a student is selected at random from Grade $10$. What is the probability that this student takes the bus? Give your answer as a decimal rounded to the nearest hundredth.
hint: The student is chosen only from Grade $10$. That condition changes the group you divide by.

hints.text: The student is chosen only from Grade $10$. That condition changes the group you divide by.
The Grade $10$ column has a total of $90$ students, and $35$ of them take the bus. Divide $35$ by $90$ and round to two decimal places.
The fraction $\dfrac{35}{90}$ is about $0.389$, so the probability is $0.39$ to the nearest hundredth.

learningObjective: Compute a conditional probability from a two-way table.
explanation: The student comes from Grade $10$, so only that column of the table matters. Its total is $90$ students.
Within Grade $10$, the number of students who take the bus is $35$.
Divide to get $\dfrac{35}{90} = 0.3888\ldots$, which rounds to a probability of $0.39$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Three denominators, three different answers
steps: Out of Grade 10: $\dfrac{35}{90} \approx 0.39$ ✓ — same numerator every time. The phrase after "from" or "of those who" names the denominator.
